skill1: Recovers 3.52% of attack damage as HP, lasts for 15 sec.
Additionally recovers 16.5% of ATK damage as HP, lasts for 15 sec.
skill2: Gains immunity to Stun for 36.95 sec.

caveats: ⚑ skill2 trigger: kit says 'Activates when the stage target appears' — a battle-start event with no matching TriggerDef. Modeled as `passive` (fires at t=0, which is what stage-target-appearance means at scope lock). The 15s duration on the 91.09% elemental-advantage buff therefore expires ~15s into the fight and never returns; a passive with a durationSec is a one-shot window, not a permanent buff.

⚑ SAME-CASTER-SLOT OVERWRITE RISK: skill1 (46.93%) and skill2 (91.09%) are both `elemAdvantageDamagePct` self-buffs from the SAME caster slot. The buff engine overwrites same-caster-slot entries, so the two are almost certainly NOT additive — the first Full Burst inside the opening 15s likely REPLACES the 91.09% with 46.93%, a net LOSS. Whether the kit intends them to stack (separate buff identities) is not derivable from the prose; measure a real fight before trusting either number.

⚑ Burst block 3 gate: 'if the skill user has immunity to Stun' is satisfied by skill2's own 36.95s immunity, so the +5.04s Full Burst extension is live only for roughly the first 37s of a 180s fight. No schema primitive expresses a self-status window, so this override applies the extension on EVERY burst cast — it OVER-CREDITS full-burst duration for the remaining ~143s. Recipe: add a self-status gate (targetStatus is enemy-only) or drop the block after the first rotation; measure FB duration late-fight to confirm.

⚑ fillGauge 98.56% is authored as `passive`, which fires once at setup — matching 'Activates 1 time(s) per battle'. If the engine re-evaluates passives, this would multiply the opening gauge; verify one burst-gauge fill event in the rotation log.

Lifesteal ('Recovers X% of attack damage as HP') has no StatKey and no HP pool at scope lock. Left unmodeled rather than encoded as `heal`: a `heal` effect would emit spurious recovery events that a teammate's on-recovery damage buff could consume, over-crediting the team. If a recovery-consumer teammate is ever paired with this unit, revisit.
partsDamagePct is inert at scope lock (partless boss) — kept for kit completeness per the schema note.
override.note: PARSER BASELINE (HYPOTHESIS — NOT a validated model). Every ⚑ below is an UNMEASURED estimate; hand-tune + record against a real fight before trusting any number. D is a Wind SMG Attacker Burst III whose damage contribution is two elemental-advantage buffs plus a 426.24% burst nuke. The two elemental-advantage lines are the load-bearing modeling question (same stat, same caster slot — see caveats), and the burst's Full Burst Duration extension is gated on a self-status window the schema cannot express, so it is currently over-credited past ~37s. Lifesteal and stun immunity are deliberately unmodeled (no HP pool, no self-status primitive); the stun-immunity line is NOT decorative — it is the gate for the burst's third block.

flags.reasoning: 'Activates when the stage target appears' is a battle-start event with no matching TriggerDef in the schema. At scope lock the stage target is present from the opening frame, so passive is the faithful stand-in. This is an INVENTED trigger (ALWAYS-⚑ category 2) — the kit gives an activation clause the vocabulary cannot express, not a damage line with no trigger, but the same honesty rule applies.
flags.recipe: Read the opening ~2s of a real fight: confirm the burst gauge jumps to ~98.56% before any shot lands (t=0 fill) rather than after a delay. If the fill is delayed, the trigger is a real stage-enter event and needs an engine primitive.

flags.estimate: Treat as OVERWRITING (net 46.93% after the first Full Burst inside the opening 15s), not additive 138.02%
flags.reasoning: Both are elemAdvantageDamagePct self-buffs from the same caster slot; the buff engine's documented behaviour is same-caster-slot overwrite. The prose gives no indication these are distinct buff identities. If they DO stack in game, this override under-credits the opening window by ~91 percentage points of Damage-Up; if they overwrite as modeled, entering Full Burst inside the first 15s is a net DPS LOSS for this unit, which is an odd kit design and worth confirming.
flags.recipe: Solo-ish fight with a forced early Full Burst (<15s): compare a normal-attack popup value just before FB entry against one just after. A drop implies overwrite (46.93 replacing 91.09); a rise implies stacking. Cross-check against a fight where FB lands after t=15s, where only 46.93% should be live.

flags.estimate: Live for the whole fight as authored; TRUE behaviour is live only for the first ~36.95s
flags.reasoning: The kit gates this on the skill user having stun immunity, which skill2 grants for 36.95 sec from battle start (once per battle). At 180s that is ~20% of the fight — after which the extension should stop. No schema primitive expresses a self-status window (targetStatus/requiresTargetStatus are enemy-only), so this block over-credits Full Burst duration on every rotation past ~37s. Full Burst duration drives every unit's damage, so this is the single largest faithfulness risk in the override.
flags.recipe: Measure Full Burst window length from footage on the FIRST rotation vs a rotation after ~40s. If the later windows are ~5s shorter, the gate is real and the block must be restricted (drop it after rotation 1, or add a self-status gate to the schema). If all windows are equal, stun immunity is either permanent or the gate is trivially satisfied and the block stands as authored.

flags.reasoning: ALWAYS-⚑ category 1: rate_of_fire and reloadFrames are known-unreliable datamine fields, and the effective rate is 60/ceil(60/nominal) on 60fps frame boundaries, not the nominal figure. No cadence override is authored here (nothing in the kit modifies it), but any downstream shot-count reasoning inherits the datamine's unreliability.
flags.recipe: Read the ammo counter across one magazine in footage to get shots/sec directly — the instrument that measures the disputed quantity, not one downstream of it.

flags.reasoning: Lifesteal has no StatKey and the v1 boss deals no damage, so there is no HP pool to restore. Encoding it as `heal` would be actively WRONG in a team context: heal emits recovery events, which fire a teammate's `recovery` trigger (e.g. an on-recovery damage buff), manufacturing damage the kit never grants. Skipping is the faithful choice, but it is a real cross-unit modeling decision, not a trivial drop.
flags.recipe: If this unit is ever paired with a recovery-consumer teammate, re-open: determine whether in-game lifesteal counts as 'recovery' for those kits' triggers, then either add the heal effects or document the exclusion.
